criteria.text: The patient has enrolled onto EAY191 and has been given a treatment assignment to ComboMATCH to EAY191-N5 based on the presence of an actionable mutation as defined in EAY191
The patient has a HER2 amplified solid tumor except breast cancer.
If IHC is 0 or 1+, the patient is not eligible.
If IHC is 3+, the patient is eligible.
If IHC is 2+, ISH/FISH or NGS must be positive for the patient to be eligible.
The patient has recurrent or persistent disease.
The patient has no known evidence of RB1 loss or deletion including copy number loss or deleterious mutation.

The patient has disease that can be safely biopsied and agrees to a pre-treatment biopsy or, if disease cannot be safely biopsied, has archival tissue available from within 12 months prior to the date of registration on the ComboMATCH Registration Trial (EAY191).
The patient has measurable disease based on RECIST 1.1. A second measurable lesion outside of the biopsiable lesion is required.

Patients with treated brain metastases are eligible if follow up brain imaging after central nervous system (CNS) directed therapy shows no evidence of progression for 3 months or more and patient is not on steroids and is asymptomatic.
The patient has no known leptomeningeal disease.
The patient has received up to 5 prior lines of systemic therapy.
Prior therapy with trastuzumab or pertuzumab, either alone or in combination, antibody drug conjugates (ADC) such as DS8201a or T-DM1 is allowed.
The patient has no prior therapy with HER2 targeting tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) such as neratinib or tucatinib.
The patient has no prior therapy with CDK4/6 inhibition.

The patient has no cancer directed therapy within 3 weeks prior to registration. For oral therapy, the washout can be reduced to greater than or equal to 5 half lives of the drug. No HER2 targeting ADCs within 30 days prior to registration.
The patient is age ≥ 18.
The patient has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of ≤ 2.
The patient is not pregnant and not nursing.
The patient has an Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1,500 cells/mm^3.
The patient has Platelets ≥ 100,000 cells/mm^3.
The patient has Hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dl.
The patient has a Creatinine clearance (CrCL) of ≥ 30 mL/min by the Cockcroft-Gault formula.
The patient has a Total bilirubin level ≤ 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN).
The patient has Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) ≤ 3 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN).

Patients with known history or current symptoms of cardiac disease, or history of treatment with cardiotoxic agents, should have a clinical risk assessment of cardiac function using the New York Heart Association Functional Classification. To be eligible for this trial, patients should be class 2B or better.
The patient has no active infection requiring parenteral antibiotics.

The patient has no current evidence of intra-abdominal abscess, abdominal/pelvic fistula (not diverted), gastrointestinal perforation, gastrointestinal (GI) obstruction, and/or need for drainage nasogastric or gastrostomy tube.

The patient has no current evidence of malabsorption or chronic diarrhea or any other significant gastro-intestinal disease (e.g gastrectomy, ileal bypass, Crohn's disease, gastroparesis), associated with moderate to severe diarrhea (grade 2 or more) or inability to tolerate oral therapy.
The patient has no lung disease causing dyspnea at rest.
The patient has no interstitial lung disease with ongoing signs and symptoms at the time of registration.
The patient has no history of allergic reaction to the study agents, compound of similar chemical or biologic composition of the study agents or any of their excipients.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "Testing the Use of Neratinib or the Combination of Neratinib and Palbociclib Targeted Treatment for HER2+ Solid Tumors (A ComboMATCH Treatment Trial)". Your earlier answers already covered 8 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you been enrolled in the EAY191 study and assigned to the ComboMATCH arm (EAY191-N5)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what the EAY191 study is. I haven't heard of it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you been diagnosed with a solid tumor that is HER2 amplified, excluding breast cancer? (HER2 is a protein found on some cancer cells. If you aren't sure, that's okay.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I haven't been told about HER2 amplification in my report.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Has your doctor ever told you that your tumor is 'HER2 positive' or 'HER2 amplified'? This is a specific test result for certain cancers. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I haven't been told about HER2 positivity in my report.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you know if your tumor testing showed an IHC score of 0 or 1+? (IHC is a scale used to measure HER2 protein levels. If you aren't sure, that's okay.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I haven't been told about an IHC score for my tumor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Has your doctor ever mentioned that your tumor has an RB1 loss, deletion, or mutation? (RB1 is a gene that helps control cell growth. If you aren't sure, that's okay.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I haven't been told about RB1 status in my report.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you haven't been told about RB1 status, do you know if your doctor has ever mentioned that your tumor has an RB1 loss, deletion, or mutation? (RB1 is a gene that helps control cell growth. If you aren't sure, that's okay.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I haven't been told about RB1 status in my report.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Would you be willing to have a biopsy before starting treatment, or do you have tumor tissue samples from a biopsy done in the last 12 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have tissue samples from the last 12 months. I had a biopsy at diagnosis, but I'm not sure if that was recent enough.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Would you be willing to have a new biopsy before starting treatment if needed?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm a pharmacist, so I understand the importance of accurate tissue for testing. I would be willing to have a new biopsy if it's necessary for the trial.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever received treatment with trastuzumab or pertuzumab, either alone or together? (These are common targeted therapies for HER2+ cancers.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I haven't had trastuzumab or pertuzumab. I only had entrectinib (Rozlytrek) for my ROS1 fusion.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever taken neratinib or tucatinib? These are targeted pills for HER2+ cancers.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't taken neratinib or tucatinib. I only had entrectinib (Rozlytrek) for my ROS1 fusion.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever taken any CDK4/6 inhibitor medications? These are a type of targeted therapy often used for breast cancer, such as palbociclib, ribociclib, or abemaciclib.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't taken any CDK4/6 inhibitors like palbociclib or ribociclib. My only prior targeted therapy was entrectinib for my ROS1 fusion.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: When was your last cancer treatment? We need to make sure it was more than 3 weeks ago (or 30 days if it was a specific type called an ADC).

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: My last treatment was entrectinib, which was more than 3 weeks ago. I haven't had an ADC.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 45 years old.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with a heart condition or had treatment with medications that can affect the heart? If so, do you know if your heart function is classified as NYHA Class 2B or better?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if my heart function is classified as NYHA Class 2B or better. I haven't been told about that specific classification.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you currently have an active infection that requires antibiotics given by injection or IV (parenteral antibiotics)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have an active infection requiring IV antibiotics.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you currently have an abdominal or pelvic abscess, a fistula (an abnormal connection between organs), a hole in your stomach or intestines, a blockage in your digestive tract, or a tube in your stomach for drainage?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any of those abdominal or pelvic issues.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you currently have any significant stomach or intestinal conditions, such as Crohn's disease or prior stomach surgery, that cause moderate to severe diarrhea or make it hard for you to take pills by mouth?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have Crohn's disease, but I'm currently stable on Humira and not experiencing moderate to severe diarrhea. I can take pills by mouth without issue.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you currently have any lung disease that causes shortness of breath while resting?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have lung disease that causes shortness of breath while resting. I'm fully active and still working full shifts.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever had an allergic reaction to neratinib, palbociclib, or any similar medications or their ingredients?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never had an allergic reaction to neratinib, palbociclib, or their ingredients.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
